@wanex/app.rationale: Trusted application backends need one stable public facade above Runtime.
@wanex/app.evidence: application consumes the root and Phase 744 public-facade tests prove the journey.

@wanex/cli.rationale: A separately executable CLI is a real product and lifecycle boundary.
@wanex/cli.evidence: Its bin/start path is production-facing; it will consume only Runtime/App public entries.

@wanex/coding.rationale: Coding application projection and trusted repository/native composition share one product owner with an explicit renderer/Host trust boundary and a distinct five-package dependency and resource closure.
@wanex/coding.evidence: The package root is application-safe; the explicit /host subpath alone opens canonical Git repositories and owns Runtime/Storage/Workspace lifecycle. Bounded read models, command settlement, and ordered invalidations expose no trusted paths or authority objects.

@wanex/connector.rationale: External-channel contracts, host lifecycle, and packaging policy share one optional capability owner while generic secret resolution belongs to Runtime.
@wanex/connector.evidence: Connector consumes the lazy @wanex/runtime/secrets port; conformance and lifecycle tests keep Connector out of Runtime/App default closure.

@wanex/eval-harness.rationale: The broad deterministic release suite is internal verification infrastructure, not a consumer SDK.
@wanex/eval-harness.evidence: Phase 755 external fixtures prove public SDK journeys without importing Eval; no two real consumers justify a new @wanex/testing package.

@wanex/extension.rationale: A dependency-free contribution contract and deterministic resolver have multiple independent App and Assistant consumers.
@wanex/extension.evidence: The contract and static host were consolidated; App, Assistant Plugin Host, and TUI compile against the retained owner.

@wanex/local-credential-store.rationale: Local keychain references and the native credential binding form one platform security and distribution boundary shared by Assistant Host, Desktop, and TUI executables.
@wanex/local-credential-store.evidence: Phase 859 moves the sole native adapter out of Assistant Host, deletes the old subpaths, and verifies both executable consumers without adding Assistant, Storage, Web, or execution authority to this package.

@wanex/mcp.rationale: Official MCP process/network dependencies, trust, and connection lifecycle must remain outside Runtime/App cold closure.
@wanex/mcp.evidence: Official SDK 1.29.0 adapters pass stdio and stateful Streamable HTTP list/call/error/cancel lifecycle tests while distribution audit reports no Runtime/App closure violation.

@wanex/plugin.rationale: Plugin trust, install, sandbox, subprocess, and worker lifecycle require one explicit optional security boundary.
@wanex/plugin.evidence: Plugin was renamed directly, Assistant command projection moved to its application owner, and the Plugin plus Assistant Host suites pass.

@wanex/assistant.rationale: Assistant conversations, plans, goals, schedules, teams, attachments, command catalog, and renderer-safe read models form one application domain above App.
@wanex/assistant.evidence: Assistant Web, Assistant Host, Assistant Plugin Host, and TUI consume its safe root or explicit subpaths; Coding remains a separate application domain.

@wanex/assistant-plugin-host.rationale: Optional Plugin action execution projects into the Assistant command surface and has a distinct process, security, dependency, and lifecycle boundary outside the default Assistant closure.
@wanex/assistant-plugin-host.evidence: The host reconstructs active Plugin generations, publishes one immutable Assistant command catalog, owns exact-version execution, and is composed explicitly by Desktop without entering Runtime, App, Assistant Web, or TUI default closures.

@wanex/desktop.rationale: Electron introduces a distinct executable process, renderer trust boundary, native-resource closure, and packaging lifecycle that must remain outside Assistant Host and every Kernel package.
@wanex/desktop.evidence: The packaged leaf loads the real Assistant Web document from its owned ephemeral loopback Host, stages exactly one System Service and keyring binding, composes optional Plugin management with an Electron-main native directory selector and user-data install root, and proves secure startup, conversation settlement, screenshot rendering, and complete process cleanup without application node_modules.

@wanex/assistant-host.rationale: The authoritative Assistant Host owns Assistant storage, Provider, resource, schedule, Team, Web, and lifecycle composition independently of whether its client is local or remote.
@wanex/assistant-host.evidence: Desktop and TUI currently borrow its lifecycle in-process; a later remote Agent Host protocol may address the same owner without changing its package identity. Coding remains independently composed through @wanex/coding, so no generic multi-domain Host closure is claimed.

@wanex/tui.rationale: The terminal product is a distinct executable leaf with terminal-only dependencies.
@wanex/tui.evidence: It owns the TUI entry and consumes the Assistant application backend.

@wanex/assistant-ui.rationale: The browser-safe Assistant UI and client are shared by multiple product hosts and have no storage or execution authority.
@wanex/assistant-ui.evidence: Assistant Host and Desktop consume the same React/browser build while host packages retain lifecycle, storage, authentication, and execution ownership.

@wanex/protocol.rationale: Cross-language wire and durable contracts need one internal source during reconstruction.
@wanex/protocol.evidence: TS packages and the Rust system service share protocol semantics; facade audits prevent public type leakage.

@wanex/runtime.rationale: This is the product-neutral public agent execution facade.
@wanex/runtime.evidence: Phase 755 installs only @wanex/runtime in an isolated external project and proves a durable minimal-agent turn from the compiled SDK.

@wanex/storage.rationale: The package owns a transport handle and composed stores, not merely a client class.
@wanex/storage.evidence: It is the durable boundary used across Runtime and optional capabilities; Phase 746 removes the universal inheritance chain.

@wanex/storage-control-plane.rationale: Authenticated server-derived store routing is an optional deployment and security boundary with an independent HTTP lifecycle.
@wanex/storage-control-plane.evidence: The Phase 755 packed external consumer proves bearer authentication, forbidden client store selection, per-subject isolation, pooled transport cleanup, and Runtime over remote HTTP.

@wanex/team.rationale: Conversation and coding delegation are separate policies over one optional multi-agent orchestration owner.
@wanex/team.evidence: Three package identities were consolidated into conversation and delegation subpaths; 23 owner tests pass.

@wanex/workspace.rationale: Filesystem mutation, review, isolation, Git, and durable workspace tasks share one optional security and release owner.
@wanex/workspace.evidence: Seven package identities were consolidated into focused Workspace modules; 43 owner tests and downstream Eval checks pass.

@wanex/product.rationale: Product described an architectural role rather than the Assistant domain actually owned by the package.
@wanex/product.evidence: The package, source directory, APIs, wire kinds, consumers, and governance moved directly to @wanex/assistant without an alias or forwarding package.

@wanex/web.rationale: The implementation renders only the Assistant application surface and was not a generic Web owner.
@wanex/web.evidence: The package and directory moved directly to @wanex/assistant-ui without an alias or forwarding package.

@wanex/local-host.rationale: The closure owned the Assistant lifecycle rather than a generic multi-domain Agent Host.
@wanex/local-host.evidence: Route 1 first moved the package to the Assistant domain; Route 1.1 then removed the misleading placement qualifier. No old package, bin, route, environment variable, or compatibility alias remains.

@wanex/assistant-local-host.rationale: Local described one possible client-to-Host placement even though the authoritative Assistant Host can be controlled by local or later remote clients.
@wanex/assistant-local-host.evidence: The unpublished package, directory, bin, public Host API, wire discriminants, scripts, consumers, and governance moved directly to @wanex/assistant-host without an alias, forwarding package, or dual decoder.

@wanex/plugin-command-host.rationale: The host projects Plugin actions specifically into the Assistant command surface.
@wanex/plugin-command-host.evidence: The package, directory, host API, composition port, and status discriminants moved directly to @wanex/assistant-plugin-host without compatibility aliases.

@wanex/command-host.rationale: The generic identity obscured that this optional host owns only plugin-backed Product commands.
@wanex/command-host.evidence: The package was renamed directly and its second Product Shell API was deleted without a forwarding package or alias.

@wanex/memory-runtime.rationale: Compaction and memory maintenance are Runtime job modules.
